slot.brief: Ask which of the given aqueous ions (e.g. Sc3+, Ti3+, Cu+, Zn2+, V3+) is colourless and why, or which listed ion shows a stated colour.

stem: Transition metal ions generally exhibit colour in aqueous solution due to $d\text{--}d$ transitions. Which of the following ions is colourless?

verdicts.working: d-electron counts: Ti3+ = d1, V3+ = d2, Sc3+ = d0, Cu2+ = d9. Colour from d–d transitions requires partially filled d orbitals; Sc3+ has empty d (d0), so no d–d transition and it is colourless.

working:
The colour of transition metal ions in aqueous solution arises from $d\text{--}d$ transitions, where an electron is promoted from a lower-energy $d$-orbital to a higher-energy $d$-orbital (e.g., $t_{2g} \to e_g$ in octahedral hydrated complexes) upon absorption of light in the visible spectrum.

For $d\text{--}d$ transitions to be possible, the metal ion must possess a partially filled $d$-subshell ($3d^1$ to $3d^9$). Ions with an empty $d$-subshell ($3d^0$) or a completely filled $d$-subshell ($3d^{10}$) cannot undergo $d\text{--}d$ transitions and are therefore colourless.

Let us determine the electronic configurations of the given ions:
1. $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ($Z = 22$): $\text{Ti} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^2 4s^2 \implies \text{Ti}^{3+} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^1$. It has one $d$-electron ($t_{2g}^1 e_g^0$) and exhibits a purple/violet colour.
2. $\text{V}^{3+}$ ($Z = 23$): $\text{V} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^3 4s^2 \implies \text{V}^{3+} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^2$. It has two $d$-electrons and exhibits a green colour.
3. $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ($Z = 21$): $\text{Sc} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^1 4s^2 \implies \text{Sc}^{3+} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^0$. It has an empty $d$-subshell; with no $d$-electrons available for transitions, $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ is colourless.
4. $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($Z = 29$): $\text{Cu} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^{10} 4s^1 \implies \text{Cu}^{2+} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^9$. It has a partially filled $d$-subshell and exhibits a blue colour.

Therefore, $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ is colourless.

Independent check: d-electron counts: Ti3+ = d1, V3+ = d2, Sc3+ = d0, Cu2+ = d9. Colour from d–d transitions requires partially filled d orbitals; Sc3+ has empty d (d0), so no d–d transition and it is colourless.
